newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end at new record, FOMC clears doubt.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end at new record, FOMC clears doubt.

text.p: Mexican shares pared some earlier gains, but ended firm at their second record close in a row on Wednesday.

Traders and analysts said the Federal Open Market Committee decision not to change U.S. interest rates had already been discounted, but propped up the market as it cleared the way for company fundamentals to boost prices.
Final closing prices placed the blue chip IPC index
up 50.44 points on the day, or 1.12 percent, at a new record of 4,559.23.

"The market had been discounting the FOMC decision for some days, but it helps to clear away extraneous factors and allows us to start looking forward to improved earnings for the second quarter," said Francisco Blanco, head of research at the Arka brokerage.
"The FOMC came as no surprise, and did not boost the market there and then, but it is still firm and foreign investors are still pouring in," a desk trader said.
Brisk trading volume of 116.3 million shares reflected keen interest by investors during the session.

The IPC had gained sharply to an intraday record of 4,579.03 in early trade following an unexpected fall in domestic interest rates amid market forecasts mid-term elections on July 6 would go ahead smoothly, analysts said.
"The fall in Cetes rates jumped ahead of a low inflation outlook and an electoral process with no great problems, and that helped," Blanco added.
Banco de Mxico placed bellwether 28-day Cetes at 19.95 percent at Tuesday night's primary auction, a fall of 95 basis points since last week.

Mexicans vote on Sunday for a new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time, a mayor of Mexico City. Previously, that post has been filled by a presidential nominee.
Dealers said financial groups in general and market heavyweight Telfonos de Mxico in particular drove the rally.
Shares listed by Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial firms, rose 8 centavos to 2.50 pesos as lower interest rates eased the banking division's past-due loans burden.
Telecom Telfonos de Mxico (Telmex) climbed 32 centavos to 19.54 pesos, boosted by Santander Investment raising the stock's weighting in its telecoms portfolio.
Traders also noted a stronger performance by construction firms Empresas ICA and Grupo Tribasa.
"Nothing has been confirmed, but official announcements made last week suggest debts held by highway concessionaires, like ICA and Tribasa, may be restructured soon," Blanco said.
ICA shares rose 6.50 pesos to 135.00 pesos, while Tribasa ended up 2.20 pesos to 23.50 pesos and headed the percentage gainers' list.
On the broad market, gainers far outpaced decliners by 73 to 30 out of 122 stocks that changed hands.
